Subject: Initial DPA redlines — use of data for model improvements

Sergio —

Thanks for sending the standard DPA. We've attached a redline with a few asks specific to data use for model improvements and subprocessor visibility. Our main concerns:

- Explicit prohibition on using customer data for training or model improvement unless expressly permitted in a separate addendum.
- Stronger definitions for "Customer Data" and examples of what constitutes PII vs. derived artifacts.
- Requirement for a current subprocessor list and 30-day notice for additions.
- Data residency/transfer paragraph to ensure EU data is processed in compliance with SCCs.

I've highlighted the two clauses in the attached PDF where we'd like explicit carve-outs. If Redwood is comfortable, we'd prefer to do execution via DocuSign — I've included a tentative envelope link at the end of this thread once we have agreed language.

Thanks — got the redlines. Looping in Monica (legal) and Evelyn (privacy) to draft a focused response. Two quick points from product/legal perspective:

1) We are open to a carve-out that prevents indiscriminate training on raw customer content — Redwood's default is not to use customer data for model improvement unless the customer explicitly opts in.

2) We need to offer a controlled alternative for customers who want opt-in training (e.g., dedicated collection, opt-in flag, clear data minimization steps).

Monica / Evelyn — can you weigh in on the proposed language? Also, McGraw has asked for a subprocessor list and 30-day notice for additions — we currently publish a regular subprocessor list and offer 14-day operational notice for most infra changes; would procurement accept 30 days?

Hi all —

Thanks for the redlines. I've attached our counter-redline and suggested compromise language (see section 3.2 and defined term "Model Improvements"). Key points in our proposed wording:

- Define "Customer Data" to explicitly include only data submitted through the API or uploaded to the customer's dedicated environment; derived metadata and aggregated telemetry will be considered non-identifiable only when de-identified in accordance with our Data Handling Addendum.

- Proposed carve-out: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data for the purpose of improving or training its general-purpose models, unless Customer provides an explicit written opt-in. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use anonymized and aggregated operational telemetry (not containing PII or Customer Data) to maintain and debug services."

- Subprocessors: we will provide an up-to-date subprocessor registry (link in our footer) and agree to 30-day notice for additions that materially affect data processing scope; for low-risk infra vendors we can keep 14-day operational notice with prior notification.

- Execution: we propose DocuSign for signature. Draft envelope and link added once language is agreed.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_DPA_response_redline.pdf (PDF, 95KB)]

Neha — can you confirm the SCC/data transfer paragraph for EU-resident accounts?

Thanks,

Monica/Sergio —

Thank you for the clear redline. A few follow-ups from McGrawTech:

- The carve-out language is close but we want an explicit example in the DPA showing "training" includes use in fine-tuning, pre-training, or instruction tuning pipelines. Please add those examples to the definition of "Model Improvements."

- On subprocessor notice: procurement asks for a 30-day notice for any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data; for routine infra (monitoring/ops) the 14-day approach is acceptable if specified.

- They also insist on a signed confirmation that Redwood will not use data tagged as "sensitive customer content" for any training, even anonymized, without a separate, mutually agreed addendum. We can confirm acceptance of the addendum route.

We're ready to proceed with DocuSign once those clarifications are in the redline. I can send the envelope for signature — prefer AdobeSign/DocuSign link.

Best,
